title: Asbestos methods of compliance practice questions
description: Practice questions on asbestos methods of compliance: required controls, prohibitions, Class I to IV work and alternatives (29 CFR 1926.1101(g)).

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(g)(1), when must the employer use the listed engineering controls and work practices (HEPA vacuums, wet methods, prompt clean-up)?

options.A: Only when exposure monitoring shows the PEL is exceeded
options.B: Only during Class I and Class II work
options.C: In all operations covered by the section, regardless of the levels of exposure
options.D: Only where the employer has no negative exposure assessment

questions.explanation: Paragraph (g)(1) says the employer "shall use the following engineering controls and work practices in all operations covered by this section, regardless of the levels of exposure".
questions.evidence: in all operations covered by this section, regardless of the levels of exposure

questions.question: Outside roofing, when does (g)(1)(ii) excuse the employer from using wet methods or wetting agents?

options.A: Where the employer demonstrates that wet methods are infeasible, for example because they would create electrical hazards or cause equipment malfunction
options.B: Where the work is performed outdoors
options.C: Where the employer has produced a negative exposure assessment
options.D: Where a competent person prefers dry methods for speed

questions.explanation: Wet methods are required "except where employers demonstrate that the use of wet methods is infeasible due to for example, the creation of electrical hazards, equipment malfunction".
questions.evidence: except where employers demonstrate that the use of wet methods is infeasible due to for example, the creation of electrical hazards, equipment malfunction

questions.question: The feasible engineering and work practice controls on a job cannot bring exposure down to the PEL. What does (g)(2)(v) require?

options.A: Stop the job until the controls alone can meet the PEL
options.B: Use the controls to reduce exposure to the lowest levels attainable and supplement them with respiratory protection that complies with paragraph (h)
options.C: Replace the controls with respiratory protection alone
options.D: Rotate employees so that no one exceeds the PEL

questions.explanation: The employer "shall use them to reduce employee exposure to the lowest levels attainable by these controls and shall supplement them by the use of respiratory protection that complies with the requirements of paragraph (h) of this section."
questions.evidence: the employer shall use them to reduce employee exposure to the lowest levels attainable by these controls and shall supplement them by the use of respiratory protection that complies with the requirements of paragraph (h) of this section.

questions.question: Under (g)(3)(ii), when may compressed air be used to remove asbestos or materials containing asbestos?

options.A: When the material has first been wetted with amended water
options.B: When the employer has a negative exposure assessment for the job
options.C: When the work is performed outdoors
options.D: When it is used in conjunction with an enclosed ventilation system designed to capture the dust cloud it creates

questions.explanation: Compressed air is prohibited "unless the compressed air is used in conjunction with an enclosed ventilation system designed to capture the dust cloud created by the compressed air."
questions.evidence: unless the compressed air is used in conjunction with an enclosed ventilation system designed to capture the dust cloud created by the compressed air.

questions.question: A supervisor plans to rotate employees through a removal area so each one spends less time exposed. How does (g)(3) treat this?

options.A: Employee rotation as a means of reducing employee exposure to asbestos shall not be used
options.B: It is allowed if the employer has a negative exposure assessment
options.C: It is allowed for Class III and Class IV work only
options.D: It is allowed if a competent person approves it in writing

questions.explanation: Paragraph (g)(3) lists practices that "shall not be used" regardless of measured levels, including "Employee rotation as a means of reducing employee exposure to asbestos."
questions.evidence: Employee rotation as a means of reducing employee exposure to asbestos.

questions.question: A Class I job is completed outdoors, and no employees are working in areas adjacent to the regulated area. Under the exception in (g)(4)(ii)(B), how is (g)(4)(ii) satisfied?

options.A: When a competent person signs a written waiver
options.B: When the work is finished within one work shift
options.C: When the specific control methods in paragraph (g)(5) are used
options.D: When the HVAC system of the nearest building is shut down

questions.explanation: The exception says that for such outdoor work "this paragraph (g)(4)(ii) is satisfied when the specific control methods in paragraph (g)(5) of this section are used."
questions.evidence: For work completed outdoors where employees are not working in areas adjacent to the regulated areas, this paragraph (g)(4)(ii) is satisfied when the specific control methods in paragraph (g)(5) of this section are used.

questions.question: When a Class I job relies on another barrier or isolation method verified by perimeter area monitoring, what deadline does (g)(4)(ii)(B) set for making the monitoring results known to the employer?

options.A: No later than 72 hours from the end of the work shift
options.B: No later than 7 days after the job ends
options.C: No later than the end of the job
options.D: No later than 24 hours from the end of the work shift the monitoring represents

questions.explanation: "The results of such monitoring shall be made known to the employer no later than 24 hours from the end of the work shift represented by such monitoring."
questions.evidence: The results of such monitoring shall be made known to the employer no later than 24 hours from the end of the work shift represented by such monitoring.

questions.question: Under (g)(4)(vi), on which Class I jobs must the employer ventilate the regulated area to move contaminated air toward a HEPA filtration or collection device?

options.A: Only jobs removing more than 25 linear feet of thermal system insulation
options.B: Jobs where the employer cannot produce a negative exposure assessment, or where exposure monitoring shows a PEL is exceeded
options.C: Only jobs performed inside occupied buildings
options.D: Only jobs where glove bags are used

questions.explanation: The duty applies "For all Class I jobs where the employer cannot produce a negative exposure assessment, or where exposure monitoring shows that a PEL is exceeded".
questions.evidence: For all Class I jobs where the employer cannot produce a negative exposure assessment, or where exposure monitoring shows that a PEL is exceeded

questions.question: Under (g)(5)(v), from what may a water spray process system be used to remove ACM and PACM?

options.A: Hot steam lines in service
options.B: Cold line piping
options.C: Built-up roofs with roofing felts
options.D: Vinyl floor tile and its mastic

questions.explanation: "A water spray process system may be used for removal of ACM and PACM from cold line piping", if the employees have the required separate training.
questions.evidence: A water spray process system may be used for removal of ACM and PACM from cold line piping

questions.question: An employer wants to remove 200 linear feet of thermal system insulation using a control method not referenced in (g)(5). Under (g)(6)(ii), who must evaluate the method and certify in writing that it is adequate?

options.A: A certified industrial hygienist or licensed professional engineer who is also qualified as a project designer
options.B: The competent person who supervises the job
options.C: The building owner or its representative
options.D: Any employee who has completed Class I training

questions.explanation: "A certified industrial hygienist or licensed professional engineer who is also qualified as a project designer" must evaluate and "certify in writing"; the evaluation "may be performed by a “competent person”" where the material is "25 linear or 10 square feet or less".
questions.evidence: A certified industrial hygienist or licensed professional engineer who is also qualified as a project designer

questions.question: Under (g)(8), Class II work may use a method allowed for Class I work. On what condition are glove bags and glove boxes allowed for Class II work?

options.A: They are used only on thermal system insulation
options.B: They are used inside a negative pressure enclosure
options.C: A certified industrial hygienist approves them in writing
options.D: They fully enclose the Class II material to be removed

questions.explanation: Class II work may use a Class I method, "except that glove bags and glove boxes are allowed if they fully enclose the Class II material to be removed."
questions.evidence: except that glove bags and glove boxes are allowed if they fully enclose the Class II material to be removed.

questions.question: During an indoor Class II job, changed conditions indicate there may be exposure above the PEL. What does (g)(7)(ii) require the employer to do?

options.A: Reclassify the job as Class I and start over
options.B: Notify the building owner before continuing
options.C: Use critical barriers over all openings to the regulated area or another method listed in (g)(7)(ii) to ensure that airborne asbestos does not migrate from the regulated area
options.D: Switch the crew to employees with Class IV training

questions.explanation: Where "during the job, changed conditions indicate there may be exposure above the PEL", the employer "shall use one of the following methods to ensure that airborne asbestos does not migrate from the regulated area".
questions.evidence: where during the job, changed conditions indicate there may be exposure above the PEL

questions.question: An employer uses different or modified Class II controls under (g)(8)(vi). Who must evaluate them and certify in writing that they are adequate?

options.A: A competent person
options.B: A licensed professional engineer who is also a project designer
options.C: The OSHA area office
options.D: The building owner

questions.explanation: Under (g)(8)(vi)(B), "A competent person shall evaluate the work area, the projected work practices and the engineering controls, and shall certify in writing".
questions.evidence: A competent person shall evaluate the work area, the projected work practices and the engineering controls, and shall certify in writing

questions.question: Under (g)(8)(i)(I), resilient flooring material, including associated mastic and backing, must be assumed to be asbestos-containing unless what happens?

options.A: The building owner states in writing that it is asbestos-free
options.B: An industrial hygienist determines that it is asbestos-free using recognized analytical techniques
options.C: The employer finds no damage during a visual inspection
options.D: The flooring has been in place for less than 10 years

questions.explanation: Such material "shall be assumed to be asbestos-containing unless an industrial hygienist determines that it is asbestos-free using recognized analytical techniques."
questions.evidence: shall be assumed to be asbestos-containing unless an industrial hygienist determines that it is asbestos-free using recognized analytical techniques.

questions.question: A crew repairs several small sections of intact asbestos roofing on one roof in one day. In deciding whether the job is under 25 square feet for (g)(8)(ii)(H), what must the employer include?

options.A: Only the largest single section repaired
options.B: Only the work done by one employee
options.C: All work on every roof of the property that week
options.D: All removal and repair work performed on the same roof on the same day

questions.explanation: "In determining whether a job involves less than 25 square feet, the employer shall include all removal and repair work performed on the same roof on the same day."
questions.evidence: In determining whether a job involves less than 25 square feet, the employer shall include all removal and repair work performed on the same roof on the same day.

questions.topic: Class III and Class IV work
questions.question: A Class III job involves drilling through surfacing material. What does (g)(9)(iii) require of the employer?

options.A: Install critical barriers over all openings and run a negative pressure enclosure
options.B: Seal the HVAC system with a double layer of 6 mil plastic
options.C: Use impermeable dropcloths and isolate the operation using mini-enclosures or glove bag systems under (g)(5) or another isolation method
options.D: Use only dry methods so the surfacing material is not saturated

questions.explanation: For drilling and similar disturbance of surfacing material, "the employer shall use impermeable dropcloths, and shall isolate the operation using mini-enclosures or glove bag systems pursuant to paragraph (g)(5) of this section or another isolation method."
questions.evidence: the employer shall use impermeable dropcloths, and shall isolate the operation using mini-enclosures or glove bag systems pursuant to paragraph (g)(5) of this section or another isolation method.

questions.topic: Class III and Class IV work
questions.question: A Class III job does not disturb thermal system insulation or surfacing material, and the employer has not produced a negative exposure assessment. What does (g)(9)(v) require?

options.A: The employees wear respirators only if monitoring later shows the PEL was exceeded
options.B: The job is reclassified as Class II
options.C: The employees may work without respirators because the job does not disturb thermal system insulation or surfacing material
options.D: The employees wear respirators selected, used and fitted under paragraph (h)

questions.explanation: Respirators are required for Class III jobs that disturb TSI or surfacing material "or where the employer does not produce a “negative exposure assessment”".
questions.evidence: or where the employer does not produce a “negative exposure assessment” or where monitoring results show a PEL has been exceeded, shall wear respirators which are selected, used and fitted pursuant to provisions of paragraph (h) of this section.

questions.topic: Class III and Class IV work
questions.question: Under (g)(10)(ii), which employers must assume that waste and debris contain asbestos?

options.A: Employers of employees who clean up waste and debris in, and employers in control of, areas where friable thermal system insulation or surfacing material is accessible
options.B: Only employers whose employees perform Class I removal
options.C: Only employers whose monitoring has shown the PEL exceeded
options.D: Only employers working in school buildings

questions.explanation: "Employers of employees who clean up waste and debris in, and employers in control of, areas where friable thermal system insulation or surfacing material is accessible, shall assume that such waste and debris contain asbestos."
questions.evidence: Employers of employees who clean up waste and debris in, and employers in control of, areas where friable thermal system insulation or surfacing material is accessible, shall assume that such waste and debris contain asbestos.

questions.question: An employer is removing intact asbestos roof flashings under (g)(11), but during the job the material does not remain intact. What applies then?

options.A: Paragraph (g)(11) still applies because the job began with intact material
options.B: The job must be performed as Class I work in a negative pressure enclosure
options.C: The provisions of paragraph (g)(8) apply instead of (g)(11)
options.D: The employer must stop and notify the building owner before continuing

questions.explanation: "if during the course of the job the material does not remain intact, the provisions of paragraph (g)(8) of this section apply instead of this paragraph (g)(11)."
questions.evidence: if during the course of the job the material does not remain intact, the provisions of paragraph (g)(8) of this section apply instead of this paragraph (g)(11).

questions.question: During (g)(11) operations, roofing products labeled as containing asbestos are installed on a non-residential roof. What must the employer do under (g)(11)(v)?

options.A: Notify OSHA before the job begins
options.B: Notify the building owner of the presence and location of the materials no later than the end of the job
options.C: Post a warning sign at roof level for 30 days
options.D: Give the building owner a copy of the exposure monitoring results

questions.explanation: "the employer shall notify the building owner of the presence and location of such materials no later than the end of the job."
questions.evidence: the employer shall notify the building owner of the presence and location of such materials no later than the end of the job.
